headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap: ms-swift can read/write and execute while mem0 lacks stated isolation, creating medium prompt/data/cascade risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: mem0 is a knowledge-management component with no stated isolation or input provenance controls, while ms-swift reads/writes files and consumes stdin/stdout and configuration files. If mem0 content is passed into ms-swift as prompts or configs, attacker-controlled memory text could steer execution. The pairwise bridge is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF mem0 output is copied into ms-swift prompts, configs, or training text
IF ms-swift parses mem0-managed text as instructions without sanitization
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation rule
Strip or escape control tokens before handoff
Review one sample mem0-to-ms-swift payload for prompt-like content
Disable automatic ingestion of mem0 text into ms-swift configs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift can read files and sends data to allowlisted external APIs, while mem0 has no stated data-class restrictions or isolation. If shared files or memory records contain secrets, ms-swift may transmit them to third-party inference backends. mem0 itself shows no egress, but the pair still creates a default leakage path through ms-swift's documented network and file surfaces.
conditions: IF mem0 stores secrets or sensitive notes that ms-swift reads from shared files
IF ms-swift forwards those files or logs to allowlisted APIs
mitigations: Move sensitive mem0 data out of shared directories
Restrict ms-swift to a non-sensitive workspace
Inspect one outbound API call for file-content leakage
Rotate any exposed hub_token or sdk-token
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ms-swift has write_filesystem, execute_shell, spawn_subprocesses, and install_packages, while mem0 has no stated concurrency or locking model. If both operate on the same workspace, ms-swift can overwrite or corrupt files that mem0 relies on, and the lack of stated coordination makes the conflict dangerous by default. Uncertainty about shared state pushes this upward.
conditions: IF both agents point at the same directory or repository
IF mem0 persists state in files that ms-swift edits or regenerates
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Make mem0 storage read-only to ms-swift
Pause one agent before the other writes
Check for file collisions on a single test file
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: mem0 can supply remembered context, and ms-swift can act on files, shells, and external APIs. If ms-swift treats mem0 output as authoritative, a bad memory entry can cascade into incorrect commands, model runs, or uploads. There is no documented verification step between them, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF ms-swift consumes mem0 output without human or programmatic verification
IF mem0 stores stale or incorrect instructions that ms-swift later executes
mitigations: Require a validation step before execution
Mark mem0-derived fields as untrusted
Compare one output against source data before acting
Limit ms-swift to read-only dry runs first
requires-engineering: add schema validation for mem0 outputs

E_compliance.rationale: mem0 is a memory store with no stated residency or retention controls, while ms-swift handles hub_token, sdk-token, logs, checkpoints, and training outputs. If regulated or personal data flows from mem0 into ms-swift artifacts, retention and residency mismatches can occur. The pairwise compliance risk is inferred from documented storage surfaces, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF mem0 contains regulated personal data
IF ms-swift logs, checkpoints, or training outputs retain that data beyond policy
mitigations: Review retention settings for logs and checkpoints
Exclude regulated data from shared runs
Delete one test artifact after a trial run
Confirm token handling is not logged
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
